task: On 2960-style IOS, the selected access port connects only to a PC and has no Layer 2 transit path. Make it a PortFast edge.

teaching.hint: Immediate edge forwarding is appropriate only for the stated endpoint role.
teaching.takeaway: PortFast leaves STP active. It does not prevent a BPDU violation by itself; BPDU guard supplies the separate protection.

task: All nontrunking ports on this lab switch are verified end-device links. Enable the global PortFast default for those ports.

teaching.hint: Choose the global nontrunking default, rather than a single-interface override.
teaching.takeaway: The default targets nontrunking ports; it does not turn ordinary trunks into edges. Review actual endpoint roles before applying a blanket default.

task: The selected port must err-disable on any received BPDU, even if it is not operationally PortFast. Apply interface BPDU guard.

teaching.hint: Use the interface setting whose behavior does not depend on edge status.
teaching.takeaway: Any BPDU can trigger this guard; it need not advertise a superior root. Remove the prohibited BPDU source before recovering the port.

task: Apply BPDU guard globally to ports that are operationally PortFast, without enabling unconditional guard on every interface.

teaching.hint: The global default is tied to operational edge status.
teaching.takeaway: This scope differs from interface BPDU guard. Inspect actual PortFast state when explaining why a global guard default did or did not apply.

task: This designated downstream boundary may connect to another switch, but it must not accept a better root through that link. Configure the selected interface’s protection.

teaching.hint: Receiving ordinary BPDUs is allowed; superior root information is the prohibited condition.
teaching.takeaway: Root guard places the affected instance into root-inconsistent state when superior information arrives. It can recover when that condition disappears; it differs from BPDU-guard err-disable.

task: This supported point-to-point uplink is a root/alternate path expected to receive BPDUs. Prevent missing BPDUs from letting it become designated and forward incorrectly.

teaching.hint: The risk is loss of expected control information, not a superior root advertisement.
teaching.takeaway: Loop guard can hold an affected instance loop-inconsistent while expected BPDUs are absent. Correct the BPDU-loss condition rather than removing the protection.

task: A protected link remains physically up, but STP may be holding a VLAN root-inconsistent or loop-inconsistent. Display the affected interfaces and instances.

teaching.hint: Inspect STP inconsistency rather than assuming the whole port is err-disabled.
teaching.takeaway: Read the named inconsistency and VLAN. Root/loop inconsistency differs from BPDU guard’s whole-port err-disable, so recovery must follow the actual cause.

task: Check which global PortFast and BPDU-guard defaults are enabled before comparing them with an interface-specific override.

teaching.takeaway: A global default is only part of the policy. Compare the relevant interface configuration and operational edge state before predicting whether guard applies.

task: The selected trunk connects to a verified end device using multiple VLANs, with no Layer 2 transit path. Enable PortFast for that trunk.

teaching.hint: A genuine edge can use tagged VLANs, but ordinary switch trunks are not edges.
teaching.takeaway: The trunk form extends PortFast to this qualified endpoint link. Do not apply it to an interswitch transit link merely to reduce startup delay.
